diagnostics.notes: Claims verified against their own abstracts; both extractions are faithful. Side A reports 1-year overall survival after curative HCC therapy (OR1yr=2.62, P<0.00001); Side B reports median progression-free survival in TACE-treated (non-curative) patients (12 vs 7 months, P=0.0016). Outcomes differ (OS vs PFS) and treatment settings differ (curative vs TACE non-curative), so no comparable contrast exists.

source_evidence.quote: Treatment with metformin was associated with significantly longer OS (OR1yr=2.62, 95%CI: 1.76-3.90; OR3yr=3.14, 95%CI: 2.33-4.24; OR5yr=3.31, 95%CI: 2.39-4.59, all P<0.00001) and RFS (OR1yr=2.52, 95%CI: 1.84-3.44; OR3yr=2.87, 95%CI: 2.15-3.84; all P<0.00001; and OR5yr=2.26, 95%CI: 0.94-5.45, P=0.07) rates vs. those of other anti-hyperglycemic agents after curative therapies for HCC.
For the whole cohort, the median OS (42 vs 32 months, p=0.054) and PFS (12 vs 7 months, P=0.0016) were longer in the metformin group than that in the non-metformin group.

verdict.label: not_comparable
verdict.rationale: Side A's claim concerns 1-year overall survival after curative HCC treatment (metformin vs other anti-hyperglycemic agents, OR1yr=2.62, P<0.00001), while Side B's claim concerns median progression-free survival in TACE-treated (non-curative) HCC patients (12 vs 7 months, P=0.0016). The outcome measures (OS vs PFS) and treatment settings (curative vs TACE non-curative) differ, so the two findings do not address a sufficiently similar outcome or contrast. Both extractions were verified as faithful to their sources.
